audit_items.reason: SPECIFICATION-ONLY: get_data_column_sidecars_from_block is a consensus layer specification function (SG-004/validator) for PeerDAS that does not have a direct implementation in the Nethermind EL client. This property relates to Merkle proof construction in the CL beacon client, not EL node implementation.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar is a consensus layer networking specification function for PeerDAS gossip subnet mapping. This is implemented in CL beacon clients (Lighthouse, Prysm, etc.), not the Nethermind EL client.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS sidecar retention is a CL validator duty specification. Data column sidecar storage and serving is handled by consensus layer beacon clients, not EL nodes like Nethermind.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: bytes_to_bls_field BLS_MODULUS validation is a cryptographic primitive in the consensus specs KZG library. Nethermind relies on external CKZG library (ckzg-4844) for KZG operations which handles this validation internally. The check is for spec-level validation, not EL client code.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff (SG-019) is a consensus specs function for PeerDAS proof generation. Nethermind uses the external CKZG library which wraps c-kzg-4844. Performance characteristics are determined by the cryptographic library implementation, not the EL client.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Trusted setup ceremony documentation and trapdoor compromise documentation is a specification-level concern. This relates to the KZG ceremony conducted by the Ethereum Foundation, not any client implementation code.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Batch verification with Fiat-Shamir challenge for tampered evaluation data detection is a CL cryptographic verification function. The pairing-based verification is implemented in the CKZG library used by the spec, not directly in Nethermind EL code.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Proof reuse attack prevention via Fiat-Shamir challenge binding is a cryptographic property of the KZG scheme defined in consensus specs. This is verified by the underlying CKZG library's cryptographic primitives, not EL client code.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Mutually inconsistent recovery cell detection and post-recovery verification is a CL data availability sampling function. The recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs function is part of consensus specs, not Nethermind EL implementation.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Network topology attack analysis and subnet censorship resilience is a CL networking concern. Custody group distribution across subnets is managed by beacon nodes in the P2P layer, not EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Sidecar request rate-limiting is a CL validator P2P networking concern. Rate-limiting for data column sidecar serving is implemented in beacon clients (Lighthouse, Prysm, etc.), not Nethermind EL.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Privacy of custody group membership via column serving behavior is a CL validator operational concern. This timing side-channel analysis applies to beacon node implementations, not EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Custody requirements computation from finalized state is a CL beacon state function. get_custody_columns uses beacon state effective balances, which is a consensus layer function not present in EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: blobs_bundle.proofs length validation before slicing is an Engine API concern at the CL-EL boundary. While Nethermind implements Engine API, this specific validation is for the CL side receiving the blob bundle from block production.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Merkle proof generalized index for blob_kzg_commitments in Fulu BeaconBlockBody is a CL SSZ structure concern. The generalized index computation is part of beacon client implementations, not EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Inverse FFT bit-reversal polynomial degree verification is a cryptographic function in the consensus specs polynomial commitment scheme. This is implemented in the CKZG library, not EL client code.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Recovery performance with minimum cells (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2) is a CL data availability sampling performance characteristic. The recover_polynomialcoeff function performance is determined by the CKZG library, not EL code.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Division by zero in recovery due to PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY and coset overlap is a cryptographic implementation concern in the CKZG library. This is not directly implemented in Nethermind EL code.
SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Data withholding attack detection via sampling is a CL data availability sampling protocol concern. This is handled by beacon clients performing DAS, not EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT floor for low-balance validators is a CL beacon state function. Custody assignment is computed from validator effective balances in beacon state, not EL state.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Bit-reversal permutation (BRP) consistency across polynomial_eval_to_coeff, coset_shift_for_cell, coset_for_cell, and recover_polynomialcoeff is a cryptographic library implementation concern. These functions are in CKZG, not Nethermind EL.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Batch verification resource cost bounding for verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch is a CL cryptographic library concern. Batch size limits are determined by the CKZG library implementation, not Nethermind EL code.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: hash_to_bls_field collision resistance is a cryptographic primitive defined in the consensus specs. The hash function security is a property of the cryptographic library, not EL client implementation.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Pairing check soundness e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) for KZG proofs is a cryptographic property verified by the CKZG library using BLS12-381 pairings. This is not directly implemented in Nethermind EL code.
SPECIFICATION-ONLY: BLS12-381 bilinear Diffie-Hellman assumption is a foundational cryptographic assumption. This is a mathematical property of the curve, not a client implementation concern.
SPECIFICATION-ONLY: total_node_balance overflow safety in custody computation is a CL beacon state computation. The balance summation occurs in beacon client implementations, not EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Fork epoch ordering (GENESIS < ALTAIR < ... < FULU) is a CL specification constant. While Nethermind has fork epoch awareness for EIP activation, the fork epoch ordering validation is primarily a CL beacon client concern.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: compute_fork_version function returning exactly one version is a CL beacon state function. Fork version computation from epoch is part of beacon client implementations, not EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: compute_fork_version edge case handling for epoch=0 and uint64_max is a CL function robustness concern. This validation occurs in beacon clients processing ENR records, not EL clients.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: extract_deposit_data pubkey offset validation as described is a Python consensus spec reference implementation detail. Nethermind's C# implementation (ExecutionRequestProcessor.cs) uses ABI decoding which handles this differently - it decodes the entire DepositEvent ABI structure rather than manual offset validation. The property references tb-002 which is about EL parsing, but the specific 'PUBKEY_OFFSET constant comparison' pattern does not exist in Nethermind's implementation.
audit_items.audit_notes: Nethermind uses _abiEncoder.Decode(AbiEncodingStyle.None, DepositEventAbi, log.Data) which validates structure via ABI parsing rather than manual offset checks. The ValidateLayout function checks field sizes but not offsets.

audit_items.reason: SPECIFICATION-ONLY: ABI-encoded deposit data offset manipulation bypass is a Python reference spec concern. Nethermind's ABI decoder handles offset validation internally through the Nethermind.Abi library's decoding logic. The attack vector described (manipulating ABI offsets to extract from unintended positions) would be caught by the ABI decoder throwing AbiException.
audit_items.audit_notes: AbiException is caught and converted to InvalidBlockException, preventing malformed ABI data from causing incorrect extraction.

audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: This check verifies consistency between Deposit Contract and EL Node deposit data extraction. The Deposit Contract is a Solidity smart contract deployed on-chain, not part of the Nethermind EL client codebase. Cross-implementation testing requires external test harnesses, not code audit.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Five-offset validation pattern (pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, signature, index) as described is a Python reference implementation detail. Nethermind's implementation validates field SIZES (not offsets) via ValidateLayout function after ABI decoding.
audit_items.audit_notes: ValidateLayout validates: PublicKeySize=48, WithdrawalCredentialsSize=32, AmountSize=8, SignatureSize=96, IndexSize=8. This is size validation, not offset validation.

audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: Deposit Contract interface encoding verification is about the Solidity contract's ABI encoding, not the Nethermind EL client. The contract is external to this codebase.

SPECIFICATION-ONLY: Individual offset mismatch rejection is a Python spec pattern. Nethermind raises InvalidBlockException for any ABI decoding failure or size mismatch, but doesn't have individual offset validation per the spec pattern.

Cross-implementation concern: Integer overflow in offset parsing for Go/Rust/Java implementations is a cross-client comparison that requires testing against multiple EL implementations. Nethermind C# uses safe integer handling via the ABI decoder.

IN-SCOPE: Nethermind implements deposit field size validation. ValidateLayout function at ExecutionRequestProcessor.cs:138-154 validates all five sizes: pubkey=48, withdrawal_credentials=32, amount=8, signature=96, index=8.

phase2_findings.notes: All five field sizes are validated with exact match requirements. Type checking ensures byte array format. InvalidBlockException thrown on any mismatch.

phase3_findings.rationale: Size validation is complete and correctly implemented. All five sizes match EIP-6110 specification constants defined in ExecutionRequestExtensions.cs.

audit_items.reason: Memory safety concern for Go/C/C++ implementations: Nethermind is written in C# which is memory-safe by default. Buffer overread via ABI size manipulation would be caught by the CLR bounds checking, not causing memory corruption. The check is more relevant to unsafe language implementations.
audit_items.audit_notes: C# Span<T> and array operations have built-in bounds checking. Any out-of-bounds access would throw IndexOutOfRangeException, not memory corruption.

audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: Deposit contract actor encoding verification is about the Solidity contract, not Nethermind EL client code. The deposit contract is external to this codebase.
IN-SCOPE: Nethermind rejects blocks containing deposits with invalid field sizes via InvalidBlockException thrown from ValidateLayout, which propagates to block rejection.

phase2_findings.notes: InvalidBlockException is thrown for size mismatches. AbiException and OverflowException are also caught and converted to InvalidBlockException.

phase3_findings.rationale: Block validation correctly rejects invalid deposits. No state changes occur on validation failure as the exception propagates up the call stack.

audit_items.reason: IN-SCOPE: Nethermind's deposit data extraction produces exactly 192 bytes (48+32+8+96+8) via buffer allocation and validated copying.

phase2_findings.notes: DepositRequestsBytesSize = 48+32+8+96+8 = 192 bytes. Buffer is pre-allocated to exact size. ValidateLayout ensures each field is correct size before copying.

phase3_findings.rationale: Output length is deterministic at 192 bytes due to pre-allocated buffer and validated field sizes. No code path can produce different lengths on success.

audit_items.reason: IN-SCOPE: Attacker cannot cause output length != 192 because buffer is pre-allocated and field sizes are validated before copying.

phase2_findings.notes: ValidateLayout runs before the copy loop, ensuring each field is exactly the expected size. Any size mismatch throws InvalidBlockException before data is copied to buffer.

phase3_findings.rationale: Validation-before-copy pattern ensures buffer is always filled with exactly 192 bytes of validated data or exception is thrown. No partial writes possible.

audit_items.reason: IN-SCOPE: EL node requests hash calculation uses flat-encoded requests which expects exactly 192 bytes per deposit.

phase2_findings.notes: Hash is computed over the raw byte arrays. Each deposit request is 192 bytes + 1 byte type prefix. The hash function (SHA256) will produce consistent hashes regardless of content.

phase3_findings.rationale: Requests hash calculation is deterministic. Any length mismatch would already have caused InvalidBlockException during deposit decoding.

audit_items.reason: IN-SCOPE: Every validation failure in DecodeDepositRequest terminates with InvalidBlockException.

phase2_findings.notes: Three exception paths: 1) AbiException from decoder, 2) OverflowException from decoder, 3) InvalidBlockException from ValidateLayout. All result in InvalidBlockException.

phase3_findings.rationale: No silent failure paths exist. All validation failures propagate as InvalidBlockException. No catch blocks suppress errors.

audit_items.reason: IN-SCOPE: InvalidBlockException from deposit validation propagates up through block processing, causing block rejection.

phase2_findings.notes: InvalidBlockException is not caught in ProcessExecutionRequests or ProcessDeposits. It propagates to BlockProcessor which rejects the block.

phase3_findings.rationale: Exception propagation is clean. No partial state modifications occur because requests array is built in temporary storage before being assigned to block.

audit_items.reason: IN-SCOPE: Nethermind processes receipts in deterministic order (array iteration) which matches receipt ordering in the block.

phase2_findings.notes: Receipt iteration is deterministic (for loop over receipts array). Log iteration within receipts is also deterministic. Order matches EIP-6110 specification.

phase3_findings.rationale: Ordering is deterministic and matches spec: receipts are processed in transaction order, logs within receipts in emission order. Cross-client consistency depends on all clients using same ordering.

audit_items.reason: Cross-client test scenario: Crafting receipt ordering to cause consensus divergence requires testing against multiple EL implementations (Geth, Besu, Erigon). This is a cross-client interoperability test, not a single-client code audit.
IN-SCOPE: Nethermind's deposit request extraction algorithm is deterministic and specification-compliant.

phase2_findings.notes: ArrayPoolList maintains insertion order. No non-deterministic data structures (HashSet, Dictionary with arbitrary keys) are used in the extraction path.

phase3_findings.rationale: Algorithm is deterministic: receipt order -> log order -> append to list. No sorting or shuffling operations.

audit_items.reason: CL-EL boundary validation: This check is about CL node validating requests hash from EL node. Nethermind is an EL client - the CL validation would be in beacon clients (Lighthouse, Prysm, etc.).
IN-SCOPE: Nethermind's deposit_requests accumulator correctly concatenates deposit data without gaps or padding.

phase2_findings.notes: ArrayPoolList.AddRange performs contiguous append. No gaps introduced. Fixed-size buffers (192 bytes) ensure no padding. Type byte (0x00) is first byte per EIP-6110.

phase3_findings.rationale: Concatenation is correct: type_byte + (deposit_1 || deposit_2 || ... || deposit_n) where each deposit is exactly 192 bytes. AddRange provides gap-free append.
